cast: sam (hero, black head, teal top, NO counter ever)
alex (best friend, black head, orange hoodie, counter 15204)
lily (sister, 10, black head, yellow top, counter 14 red / 81 YRS green)
man (stranger at the bus stop, counter 00:00:00:12 red)
maya (quiet girl in the library, counter 17842)
mother (subway, counter 42 then 41 red) and baby (counter 19801 green)

script.text: A man at the bus stop has twelve seconds left. Sam grabs his collar and pulls. A truck runs the red light. His timer spins. Twelve seconds becomes forty-one years.
What if you could see how long everyone has left?
Green means decades. Orange means years. Red means hurry. You can't see your own. Not in a mirror.
Then one morning, Lily's number drops. Eighty-one years, down to two days. Saturday, two forty. Her birthday. Forty-eight hours.

So you start testing everyone. Your best friend, Alex. Orange hoodie. You check Alex. Fifteen thousand, two hundred and four days. Mister Ortiz, the janitor. Nine thousand, four hundred and twelve. He waters the dead plant every morning. Maya, the quiet girl in the library. Seventeen thousand, eight hundred and forty-two. She writes a novel no one ever reads.

You see the mother again. Her number says forty-one. Yesterday it said forty-two. The baby still says nineteen thousand, eight hundred and one. The numbers are brightest over the people you already know. The strangers are dim. Like a light turned low. The people you love burn bright. You start doing small kindnesses. You carry boxes and hold doors. It feels good.

And then you tell Alex his number. Fifteen thousand, two hundred and four days. Forty-one years. Use them. He laughs. Then he stops. He stops applying to college. Then why bother, he says. You try to take it back. The number is in his head now.
You start sorting people. You sit next to the big numbers. You walk past the small ones. You catch yourself doing it. And you feel sick.
That night, you look in the mirror. Nothing above your head. You stand on a chair, phone up. Nothing. You can't see your own.
Saturday, two forty. Counting down. Fourteen days. Use every one. Part one. So... what would yours say?
